DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph DILG OPINION No. 118a s. 2021 OCT 04 HON. ELENA M. DIEZA Mayor, Hinabangan, Samar Office of the Mayor Hinabangan, Samar Dear Mayor Dieza: This has reference to the letter dated September 14, 2021 from Vice-Mayor Clarito Rosal requesting clarification on the following pivotal issues: 1. Can the municipal mayor validly withhold the salaries and allowances of the sanggunian members for the sole reason of failure to enact the appropriation ordinance for the current year pursuant to Section 323 of the LGC? 2. Does the term "additional remunerations" in Section 323 of the LGC include salaries and allowances of sanggunian members? 3. Is there any basis in the LGC or other laws or jurisprudence for a Local Chief Executive to compel the sanqqunian to enact an appropriation ordinance? As culled from Vice-Mayor Rosai's letter, the following are the factual antecedents: • The members of the Sangguniang Bayan (SB) of Hinabangan receive their Representation and Transportation Allowance (RATA) on the second week of each month and their salaries every 25th of the month; • In March 2021, you allegedly issued Memorandum Order No. 04, Series 2021 dated February 26, 2021 with the subject "Order Withholding the Actual Release of the Remuneration of All Sangguniang bayan Members as Provided under Section 323 ofRA 7160"; • After the issuance of the Memorandum, the sanggunian members were not able to receive their salaries and allowances. However, other employees and officials of the municipal government were able to receive their salaries and allowances without issue; • Vice-Mayor Rosal wrote your Office to inquire about the status of their RATA; Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

In your reply, you reiterated your Memorandum Order No. 04, Series 2021, which according to you is anchored on Sections 319, 323 and 44 of RA 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991 , • Hence, the herein pivotal issues which proffered by Vice-Mayor Rosai. Section 3051 of the Local Government Code of 1991 states the fundamental principle in the operations of local government units— unless and until the Appropriations Ordinance is approved, no money shall be paid out of the local treasury. This is the reason why in Section 319 of the Code the sanggunian is mandated to enact an Appropriations Ordinance, thus: "SECTION 319. Legislative Authorization of the Budget.—On or before the end of he current fiscal year, the Sanqqunian concerned shall enact. throuqh an ordinance. the annual budget of the local government unit for the ensuinq fiscal year on the basis of the estimates of income and expenditures submitted by the local chief executive." (Emphasis Supplied) This only proves that the Appropriations Ordinance is the most important piece of legislation in a local government unit. If the sanggunian fails to pass an ordinance authorizing the annual budget, Section 323 of the Code provides for the consequences: "SECTION 323. Failure to Enact the Annual Appropriations. - In case the sanggunian concerned fails to pass the ordinance authorizinq the annual appropriations at the beqinninq of the ensuinq fiscal year: it shall continue to hold sessions without additional remuneration for its members until such ordinance is approved. and no other business may be taken up durinq such sessions. If the sanqqunian still fails to enact such ordinance after ninety (90) days from the beqinninq of the fiscal year. the ordinance authorizinq the appropriations of the precedinq year shaii be deemed reenacted and shall remain in force and effect until the ordinance authorizing the proposed appropriations is passed bv the sanqqunian concerned. However, only the annual appropriations for salaries and wages of existing positions, statutory and contractual obligations, and essential operating expenses authorized in the annual end supplemental budgets for the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted and disbursement of funds shall be in accordance therewith. In the implementation of such reenacted ordinance, the local treasurer concerned shall exclude from the estimates of income for the preceding fiscal year those realized from nonrecurring sources, like national aids, proceeds from loans, sale of assets, prior year adjustments, and other analogous sources of 1 Sec. 305. Fundamental Principles. - The financial affairs, transactions, and operations of local govemment units shall be govemed by the following fundamental principles: (a) No money shall be paid out of the local treasury except in pursuance of an appropriations ordinance or law; Page 2 of 4

income. No ordinance authorizing supplemental appropriations shall be passed in place of the annual appropriations. In case the revised income estimates be less than the aggregate reenacted appropriations, the local treasurer concerned shall accordingly advise the sanggunian concerned which shall, within ten (10) days from the receipt of such advice, make the necessary adjustments or reductions. The revised appropriations authorized by the sanggunian concemed shall then be the basis for disbursements." (Emphasis Supplied) The first sentence of aforequoted provision of the Code states that if the sanggunian fails to pass an ordinance authorizing the annual budget, it shall continue to hold sessions, until such ordinance is approved and no other business may be taken up during such session. Clearly therefore, what is being required is the continuous conduct of sessions. The word "session" mentioned therein refers to either regular or special session conducted by the sanggunian and attended by all or at least the majority of the members therein sufficient to constitute a quorum. A regular session is that which has been fixed as to the day, time and place through a Resolution passed by the sanggunian concerned on the first day of the session immediately following the election its members. The minimum number of regular sessions shall be once a week for the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, Sangguniang Panlungsod, and Sangguniang Bayan, and twice a month for the Sangguniang Barangay [Section 52 (a), Local Government Code of 1991]. A special session, on the other hand, refers to that called by the local chief executive (LCE) or by a majority of the members of the sanggunian when public interest so demands [Section 52 (b), Local Govemment Code of 19911. However, in cases where the sanggunian fails to pass an ordinance authorizing the annual budget, Section 323 requires them to continuously hold session until such ordinance is approved. In conducting and attending said sessions, the sanggunian members so attending shall not receive additional remuneration. In reply therefore to Vice-Mayor Rosal's second query, the term "additional remuneration" in Section 323 of the Code pertains to the compensation received by the sanggunian members in addition to what they regularly receive and granted to them by reason only of attending the additional sessions. An example of this is the claim for additional allowances. In cases where the sanggunian fails to pass an ordinance authorizing the annual budget, sanggunian members cannot claim additional allowances for the additional sessions they have attended. While it may be argued that the term "remuneration" is a general term as to encompass the salary and benefits regularly received by the sanggunian member, note that the Code use not only the word "remuneration" but the term "additional remuneration" which implies such amount on top of what the sanggunian member regularly receives. Going back to the first query, since Section 323 only contemplates the non-payment of additional remuneration and therefore excludes the regular/basic salary and benefits received by the sanggunian member, your Office cannot validly withhold the salaries and allowances of the sanggunian members for the sole reason of failure to enact the appropriation ordinance for the current year. Hence, it appears that your Page 3 of 4

enact the appropriation ordinance for the current year. Hence, it appears that your Memorandum Order No. 04, Series 2021 went beyond what was contemplated under the Code and needs to be modified to conform to the provisions of the law. As to the third query, the action of the Sangguniang Bayan in authorizing the annual appropriations is legislative in nature and requires the collective exercise of judgment or discretion by the members thereof as opposed to the exercise of a purely ministerial function2. If the sanggunian finds that the budget proposal submitted by the local chief executive violates a law or allocates a budget lesser than what is required under pertinent laws, rules and regulations, then the sanggunian cannot be compelled to give legislative authorization. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. Please be guided accordingly. Very truly yours, By the Authority of the Secretary: AN Underse etary for Local Government LLLS/RPB/L LLD/clp Copy furnished: ATTY. ARNALDO ESCOBER, JR.
